[cast] Enable variable aspect ratio mirroring and in-band resolution

Enable variable aspect ratio and receiver-side content scaling in Cast
Web Runtime (CWR) mirroring applications, and detect in-band H.264 SPS,
VP9, and VP8 keyframe header resolution changes in
StarboardVideoDecoder:

- Set display.can_scale_content = true in CoreStreamingConfigManager so
  senders negotiate native aspect ratios without sender-side
  letterboxing.
- In StarboardVideoDecoder::CheckForInBandResolutionChange(), use a
  stack-local media::H264Parser (capped to the first 1024 bytes of
  unencrypted H.264 buffers and stopping at the first VCL slice),
  media::Vp9Parser, and RFC 6386 Section 9.1 VP8 keyframe header parsing
  to propagate mid-stream resolution changes to the media delegate and
  Starboard sample info.
- Restore container dimensions across Stop()/re-initialization while
  preserving in-band dimensions when PushBuffer() precedes Initialize().
- Add unit tests in core_streaming_config_manager_unittest.cc and
  starboard_video_decoder_test.cc.

[cast] Repair DRM test buffers with mismatched subsample sizes

Six tests in starboard_audio_decoder_test.cc and
starboard_video_decoder_test.cc declare subsamples totalling 1+2+3+4 =
10 bytes but supply only 5 bytes of buffer data, and
DrmUtilTest.VerifySubsamplesMatchSizeDetectsInvalidSizes in
drm_util_test.cc wraps invalid-subsample buffers in
DecoderBufferAdapter. DecoderBufferAdapter replaces any buffer whose
size disagrees with its subsamples with an end-of-stream buffer, to
prevent an out-of-bounds access. The decoders under test therefore
received an EoS buffer, never reached their DRM handling, and never
called WriteSample, while VerifySubsamplesMatchSize received an EoS
buffer and returned true.

Size the decoder test buffer data to match the declared subsamples, and
pass a direct CastDecoderBuffer implementation in DrmUtilTest so that
all seven tests exercise the DRM paths they were written for. No
assertion is changed or removed; these tests become strictly stronger,
since they now reach the code they assert on.

[cast] Support dynamic screen rotation in Cast Web Runtime

Support dynamic screen rotation events from Starboard in Cast Web
Runtime (CWR). Handles 0, 90, 180, and 270 degree orientations, updates
Ozone EGL surface geometry, synchronizes Aura WindowTreeHost and
CastWindowManager bounds on orientation changes, and propagates root
transforms gated on the rotation_supported renderer feature:

- In StarboardEventSource, query CobaltExtensionGraphicsApi for render
  root transform changes and dispatch window bounds and transform
  callbacks on the UI task runner.
- In RuntimeApplicationServiceImpl, read rotation_supported from
  kCastCoreRendererFeatures and pass it to CastWindowManagerAura and
  CastWindowTreeHostAura so screen rotation transforms are only applied
  when rotation_supported is enabled.
- In CastWindowTreeHostAura, apply DIP-scaled root transforms via
  SetRootTransform and update CastScreen display metrics with the
  matching display::Display::Rotation (ROTATE_90 for rc(0, 1) < 0,
  ROTATE_270 for rc(0, 1) > 0).
- In CastLayoutManager, resize non-hidden child windows to match the
  root window bounds when added or when the root window is resized.
- In GLOzoneEglCast and GLSurfaceCast, update surface dimensions on
  resize.

[cast] Filter ANGLE-only attributes in Sb_eglCreateContext

Sb_eglCreateContext forwards the caller's attribute list to the
Starboard EGL implementation. Fix two issues with how it builds that
list:

1. Ensure the forwarded list is always EGL_NONE terminated when
   attrib_list is non-null. The copy loop stops without copying a
   terminator if the caller's list is malformed, or if the terminator is
   the last entry of an odd-length list. Terminate the list explicitly
   while preserving a null attrib_list as null.
2. Filter out the thirteen ANGLE and Chromium extension context
   attributes (0x33ac..0x34f8) that ui/gl/gl_context_egl.cc can emit in
   addition to EGL_CONTEXT_OPENGL_NO_ERROR_KHR. Native Starboard EGL
   implementations reject unrecognized attributes with EGL_BAD_ATTRIBUTE
   rather than ignoring them.

[starboard] Deduce Starboard API version at runtime via dlsym

Refactor Starboard version deduction so that Cast Web Runtime deduces
the Starboard API version at runtime via dlsym symbol probing instead
of requiring compile-time preprocessor version flags:

- Isolate versioned Starboard API adapters and graphics wrappers into
  versioned shared libraries (.so.15, .so.16, .so.17 for Starboard 15+
  and unversioned libcast_starboard_adapter.so / libGL_starboard.so for
  Starboard 14 and earlier).
- Implement StarboardAdapterLoader with a dependency-injected
  LibraryLoader interface to probe Starboard 14/13, 15, 16, and 17
  symbols at runtime and load the matching adapter library.
- Export ReleaseCastStarboardApiAdapter from the adapter DSO and invoke
  it via base::AtExitManager in StarboardAdapterLoader, while restoring
  immediate unsubscription in
  CastEglPlatformStarboard::CreateDisplayType and CreateWindow to
  prevent process teardown crashes.
- Resolve Sb_* EGL functions against the local libGL_starboard DSO
  handle in Sb_eglGetProcAddress when loaded with RTLD_LOCAL, and handle
  null SbDrmSystem gracefully when DRM is unsupported on the target
  platform.
- Add unit tests in starboard_adapter_loader_test.cc,
  cast_starboard_api_adapter_test.cc, and starboard_drm_wrapper_test.cc.

      cast_starboard_api_adapter_test

Move CreateSessionServiceTabHelper to TabFeatures

Moves `CreateSessionServiceTabHelper` out of
`TabHelpers::AttachTabHelpers` into `TabFeatures::Init` and
`TabFeatures::WillDiscardContents` on Desktop, and into
`TabFeatures::TabFeatures` on Android. Also calls
`CreateSessionServiceTabHelper` in `TabModel` (so unit tests with
`PreventFeatureInitializationForTesting` still get a valid tab session
ID) and in `TabWebContentsDelegateAndroid::AddNewContents` for pre-tab
`HistoryTabHelper` initialization.

Merge repeated conditional blocks in browser_tests

browser_tests in chrome/test/BUILD.gn had several sibling blocks with
the same condition: three `if (is_win)`, three `if (!is_chromeos)`, two
`if (is_mac)` and two `if (is_win || is_mac || is_linux)`. Fold them
into a single block per condition, keeping comments next to the
entries they describe. The blocks only append to lists (plus a single
`libs` assignment), so this doesn't change the build graph.

Verified gn check on all platforms. `gn desc` deps, public_deps,
data_deps, data, sources, configs, libs and ldflags for browser_tests,
unit_tests and interactive_ui_tests are identical before and after on
Linux, Linux release, ChromeOS, Windows x64 and x86, Mac, Android
desktop and Android phone. browser_tests built on Linux.
browser_tests test lists (--gtest_list_tests) are identical before and
after on Linux (38755 tests) and ChromeOS (49012 tests).

Deduplicate equivalent endpoints in QuicSessionPool::AsyncDnsJob

When an alternative job (`quic_version_` known from Alt-Svc,
`require_dns_https_alpn == false`) resolves a host that also has a DNS
HTTPS record without ECH configs or Trust Anchor IDs,
`ServiceEndpointRequest` returns both the HTTPS `ServiceEndpoint` (with
`supported_protocol_alpns` and `target_name` metadata) and the fallback
authority A/AAAA `ServiceEndpoint` (with empty metadata).

Previously, `AsyncDnsJob::Candidate::operator==` used default equality
comparing the entire `ConnectionEndpointMetadata` struct. Even when
`GetUsableEndpoints()` selected the same QUIC version for both endpoints
and their QUIC handshakes would be identical, `TakeNextCandidate()`
treated them as distinct candidates—retrying the same failing IP before
falling back to the other address family, or allowing the secondary
connector to start a duplicate concurrent attempt to an already
in-flight IP after DNS finished.

Update `Candidate::operator==` to compare only the parameters that
affect the QUIC handshake (`ip_endpoint`, `quic_version`,
`metadata.ech_config_list`, and `metadata.trust_anchor_ids`), since
`supported_protocol_alpns` and `target_name` only participate in QUIC
version selection.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers for chromecast

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

Fix Reporting API crash attribution on Android

On Android, child processes are spawned from the system Zygote where
waitpid() cannot retrieve POSIX exit statuses. As a result,
ChildProcessLauncherHelper::GetTerminationInfo() maps all foreground
process terminations to TERMINATION_STATUS_OOM_PROTECTED.

Previously, RenderFrameHostImpl::MaybeGenerateCrashReport()
unconditionally set `reason: "oom"` for
TERMINATION_STATUS_OOM_PROTECTED. This misclassified foreground
unresponsive kills and normal crashes as OOMs (also suppressing JS call
stack attachment on unresponsive pages) and generated spurious crash
reports on clean or browser-initiated shutdowns.

The CL updates MaybeGenerateCrashReport() to correctly inspect OOM
metrics, renderer responsiveness, clean-exit state, and
browser-initiated shutdown flags for TERMINATION_STATUS_OOM_PROTECTED
status on Android.

Reland "Remove redundant browser_public_dependencies (batch 6, 4/5)"

This is a reland of commit 256f7592cfab6788f9d6259a638518154616a82f.

Removing //chrome/browser:browser_public_dependencies from
//chrome/browser/ui/views:views exposed missing generated header
dependencies in ChromeOS targets that use allow_circular_includes_from
or static_library deps (which gn check permits without propagating Ninja
order-only inputdeps):
- Add //chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash/office_fallback:mojo_bindings to
  //chrome/browser/ash/file_manager and
  //chrome/browser/ui/webui/ash/cloud_upload (fixes office_file_tasks.cc
  missing office_fallback.mojom.h on chromeos-reven-chrome).
- Move //chrome/browser/ash/fusebox:fusebox_proto to public_deps of
  //chrome/browser/ash/fusebox and add it to circular-include targets
  (file_manager, virtual_tasks, system_web_apps/apps).
- Move //chrome/browser/apps/app_preload_service/proto to public_deps
  of app_preload_service, ash/app_list, and ash/extensions.
- Move //chrome/browser/lens/core/mojom:mojo_bindings to public_deps of
  ui/ash/capture_mode and add it to ash/policy/dlp.
- Move //chrome/browser/support_tool:support_tool_proto to public_deps
  of event_based_logs and add it to ash/policy/core.

Original change's description:
> Remove redundant browser_public_dependencies (batch 6, 4/5)
>
> Remove //chrome/browser:browser_public_dependencies from targets in
> chrome/browser/ui/BUILD.gn through
> chrome/browser/ui/webui/browser_switch/BUILD.gn where it is no longer
> needed, or replace it with specific generated header dependencies.

[textdecoder] Clear JIS0212 state on EUC-JP errors

An invalid third byte in a JIS0212 sequence leaves the table selection
set, causing subsequent JIS0208 pairs in the same decoding session to
use the wrong mapping.

Clear the selection on the error path before processing the next byte.
Keep codec reuse and the existing end-of-input reset.

Remove x-frame-options-deny-multiple-clients.html

The test framed the same X-Frame-Options: deny resource twice to check
that cancelling two main resources for the same URL in
didReceiveResponse() didn't crash. That code path is long gone: XFO is
now enforced in the browser by AncestorThrottle, and navigation has
been rewritten many times since. The test has been marked
[ Failure Pass ] since 2016, and its baselines were stale (they expect
the full URL in the console message, while AncestorThrottle reports
the origin), so it was not providing meaningful coverage.

Merge repeated conditional blocks in interactive_ui_tests

interactive_ui_tests in chrome/test/BUILD.gn had several sibling
blocks with the same condition: two `if (is_win)`, three
`if (is_win || is_mac || is_linux)` and two `if (is_mac)`. Fold the
smaller blocks into a single block per condition. The blocks only
append to lists, so this doesn't change the build graph.

Verified gn check on all platforms. `gn desc` deps, public_deps,
data_deps, data, sources, configs, libs and ldflags for
interactive_ui_tests, browser_tests and unit_tests are identical before
and after on Linux, Linux release, ChromeOS, Windows x64 and x86, Mac,
Android desktop and Android phone. interactive_ui_tests built on Linux.
interactive_ui_tests test lists (--gtest_list_tests) are identical
before and after on Linux (5748 tests) and ChromeOS (5611 tests).

Revert CHECK to DCHECK in NotifyInstallingRegistration

ServiceWorkerRegistry::NotifyInstallingRegistration contains an
assertion that the registration being marked as installing is not
already present in installing_registrations_. Converting this check from
DCHECK to CHECK caused crashes in production builds when the assertion
failed.

Revert this check back to DCHECK to prevent production crashes while
preserving the assertion check in debug builds.

This fix was generated by the Crash Autofix pipeline for crash report
crash/5a6016a908400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

[bedrock]: Enable Windows Document PiP multi-display tests

BrowserNavigatorTestWithMockScreen was disabled on Windows because
replacing ScreenWin with the generic MockScreen was said to crash. On
current Windows builds the fixture does not crash in ScreenWin.

Instead, the GPU process hits Skia Graphite's
TextureProxy::validateTexture() assertion
(fInfo.canBeFulfilledBy(texture->textureInfo())) when a texture is
instantiated. The mock displays report the default RGBA_8888 output
format, but the Windows swap chain is BGRA, which is what ScreenWin
reports for real SDR displays. The GPU process restarts several times,
so each case takes 15-20 seconds or times out waiting for the first
WebUI toolbar paint.

Give the two mock displays the sRGB color space and BGRA_8888 output
formats that ScreenWin uses on Windows, and remove the Windows disable.
Both the Browser-backed and the standalone
Disposition_PictureInPicture_OpensInSameDisplay variants now run on
Windows with the non-primary display assertions unchanged.

Update the CfT smoke filters as well.

[actor] Add a no-animation option to the glic-actor-cursor flag

Add an "Enabled (no cursor movement animation)" option to the
glic-actor-cursor flag. It sets the magic cursor's minimum and maximum
move durations to 1ms, which mirrors the Disabled arm of the
DisableGlicActorUiMagicCursorAnimation Finch study.

chrome://flags stores the selected option by index, and the new option
takes the index that Disabled used to have. Users who had set the flag
to Disabled therefore need to select it again.

Run DocumentPictureInPicturePixelTest.InvokeUi_default for both the
Browser-backed and the standalone Document PiP window.

WebUI: Fix Lit template structure violations in existing templates

Update Lit .html.ts templates across the codebase to conform to stricter
template structure requirements needed by lit_template_formatter:
- Replace switch statements in getHtml() with ternary expressions.
- Ensure arrow functions returning Lit HTML templates return a single
  html`...` tagged template literal directly.
- Wrap repeat() calls inside ternary true branches in html`...`.
- Remove unnecessary bare ${html`...`} wrappers.

This is in preparation for formatting these files and for adding an
automated eslint check to detect these cases at build time.

[Read Aloud] 3. Support pausing and resuming native voice previews

Exposes ReadAloudService::PauseVoicePreview() across JNI via
ReadAloudBridge and ReadAloudNativeBridge, and updates
NativeVoicePreviewPlayback.pause() to call pauseVoicePreview() instead
of stopVoicePreview().

Previously, pausing a voice preview called stopVoicePreview(), which
cancelled the preview and tore down the playback session. With this
change, pausing transitions the preview to the PAUSED state so a
subsequent play() call resumes playback from where it left off.

bluetooth: Fix UAF in BluetoothPairingBlueZ on synchronous cancel

PairingDelegate implementations (such as DevicePairingHandler in Ash
when a system-modal pairing dialog fails to open or is immediately
dismissed) can synchronously invoke BluetoothDevice::CancelPairing() or
BluetoothAdapter::RemovePairingDelegate() from inside delegate callbacks
like DisplayPinCode(), DisplayPasskey(), or KeysEntered().

Because BluetoothDeviceBlueZ::CancelPairing() synchronously calls
EndPairing(), which resets std::unique_ptr<BluetoothPairingBlueZ>, the
active BluetoothPairingBlueZ instance is destroyed while its method or
caller is still on the stack. This causes a use-after-free when:

1. BluetoothPairingBlueZ::DisplayPinCode() or KeysEntered() accesses
   `device_` after `pairing_delegate_` returns.
2. BluetoothAdapterBlueZ::DisplayPasskey() calls
   `pairing->KeysEntered(entered)` after `pairing->DisplayPasskey()`
   synchronously destroyed `pairing`.

This CL adds a WeakPtrFactory to BluetoothPairingBlueZ and checks weak
pointer validity after external delegate and callback invocations before
accessing member state or making follow-up calls.

[gfx] Allow 1D R8 GBM buffers to exceed 2D texture dimension limit

Camera JPEG capture streams allocate 1D buffers with format DRM_FORMAT_R8
(from HAL_PIXEL_FORMAT_BLOB) where width equals ANDROID_JPEG_MAX_SIZE
and height is 1. Commit ff2c3ca968 introduced a CHECK ensuring buffer
dimensions do not exceed 16384 to prevent 32-bit overflow in 2D image
stride/size calculations. However, for 1D R8 buffers (height == 1), the
width is the total byte size which typically exceeds 16384 (e.g. 1.8MB+).
For height == 1, stride is width and size is stride * 1, which will not
overflow 32-bit calculations as long as width <= 256 MiB.

Allow 1D R8 buffers with height == 1 to have width up to 256 MiB while
maintaining the 16384 limit for 2D buffers.

R=dnicoara@chromium.org, zork@chromium.org

Fix compile failure by removing unused wizard_controller.h include

device_disabling_manager_default_delegate.cc in //chrome/browser/ash/system
does not use WizardController, but included wizard_controller.h.
This pulled in a header include chain through oobe_ui.h to
ash/webui/common/mojom/webui_syslog_emitter.mojom.h without
//chrome/browser/ash/system having a dependency on that mojom target.
When commit df5d45f0cf931 removed //chrome/browser:browser_public_dependencies
from //chrome/browser/profiles:misc, the transitive dependency was severed,
causing compilation of device_disabling_manager_default_delegate.o to fail
when webui_syslog_emitter.mojom.h was not yet generated.

Removing the unused include breaks the unwanted dependency chain and resolves
the compile failure.

[Omnibox] Load only the classic popup code in omnibox_popup.html

The classic WebUI omnibox popup page (omnibox_popup.html) loads the
omnibox_popup.js bundle, which also contains the AIM popup app, the
full WebUI omnibox app and the whole composebox. Since the popup
WebContents is preloaded for every browser window, each window pays
for parsing, evaluating and defining all of those custom elements even
though the classic popup never renders them.

Add a dedicated omnibox_popup_classic.js entry point that only imports
app.js, and bundle it as a separate rollup input so that code shared
with omnibox_popup.js ends up in shared.rollup.js. The AIM and full
popup pages, as well as the WebUI tests, keep using omnibox_popup.js.

Add a browser test that checks the classic popup page defines only
its own app, so a stray import can't silently bring the AIM and full
popup code back.

Local measurements (Linux, is_debug=false, dcheck_always_on=true), per
browser window, compared with the current code:
- Custom elements defined in the popup renderer: 81 -> 59
  (CustomElementRegistry::define: ~104 ms -> ~44 ms).
- Top-chrome renderer main thread cost over a baseline with the
  features disabled: ~305 ms -> ~220 ms.
- browser_tests (145 tests, 8 jobs pinned to 8 cores) total runtime
  regression vs. --disable-features=WebUIOmniboxPopup,
  WebUIOmniboxAimPopup: +10.0% -> +7.0%.

TAG=agy
CONV=be865bde-5d1d-4cb0-8017-6440f8dcaeb0

Original change's description:
> Check device compatibility during ChromeScreenAI library verification
>
> The ChromeScreenAI library requires SSE4.2 on x86 architectures. When
> loading the library on incompatible CPUs, dynamic linker initialization
> crashes with SIGILL.
>
> Checking device compatibility in `ScreenAIInstallState::ShouldInstall`
> is not sufficient on its own because:
> 1. It only governs background registration and periodic checks.
>    Pre-existing libraries already downloaded to disk in earlier
>    sessions remain intact and would otherwise be marked ready and
>    loaded by the browser.
> 2. Features (such as PDF OCR or Reading Mode) can trigger on-demand
>    download requests directly via `DownloadComponent()`.
>
> This change adds compatibility checks in two additional places:
> - In `VerifyLibraryVersion()`: Failing verification on incompatible
>   devices prevents selecting the library and causes ComponentInstaller
>   to delete unselected, incompatible versions from disk.
> - In `DownloadComponent()`: Fails on-demand download requests early,
>   avoiding unnecessary network traffic on incompatible devices.
>

views: Remove unnecessary Ctrl+C as an accelerator for every Label

Label::Init() registered Ctrl+C with the FocusManager so the Chrome
menu's Copy, dispatched via FocusManager::ProcessAccelerator(), could
reach a focused Label. crrev.com/c/8160720 changed
BrowserView::CutCopyPaste() to call AcceleratorPressed() on the focused
view directly, so the registration is no longer needed. Outside
BrowserView, the Ctrl+C key is delivered to the FocusManager's focused
view as usual and handled by Label::OnKeyPressed().
On macOS, Cmd+C and Edit > Copy go through the responder chain,
which sends a synthesized key event to Label::OnKeyPressed().

It put every Label, including every tab title, into Ctrl+C's
target list, which is scanned on add, remove and key press.

Add LabelSelectionTest.CopyAcceleratorNotRegistered.

Test=views_unittests --gtest_filter=LabelSelectionTest.*

Check navigation lifetime before handling URL override exceptions

The Android URL override callback can synchronously destroy the
navigation request and then report a Java exception. Check the existing
weak pointer immediately after the callback returns, before the
exception path reads prerender state. Preserve diagnostics for live
requests and the existing exception, override, and normal navigation
behavior.

Add native regression coverage for synchronous cancellation with either
callback result, exception returns without cancellation, and normal
navigation override decisions.

[ReadAloud] Report playback progress and duration in one call

Replace OnPlaybackDurationChanged on ReadAloudPlaybackControllerClient
with OnPlaybackProgressChanged(elapsed, duration). This reports both the
current elapsed playback position and estimated total duration (both in
1.0x content time) in a single IPC from the utility process to the
browser.

Key changes:
- mojom: Replace OnPlaybackDurationChanged with OnPlaybackProgressChanged.
- ReadAloudPlaybackController:
  - Run a 250ms timer during active playback (kPlaying, kBuffering) to
    periodically report elapsed time and estimated duration.
  - Report progress immediately on SetTextContent(), seek completions,
    playback halts (pause, stop, drain), and when synthesis responses
    refine total duration while idle.
  - Compute elapsed as min(seek_base_ + renderer->GetMediaTime(), duration),
    anchoring seek_base_ to target.time.start_time on seeks.
  - Deduplicate redundant progress updates.
- ReadAloudService:
  - Validate incoming progress (non-negative and elapsed <= duration),
    rejecting invalid inputs with ReportBadMessage().
  - Forward progress to delegate_->OnPlaybackProgressUpdated().
  - Remove current_duration_ tracking and decouple progress updates
    from OnWordBoundaryReached().

Avoid crash when activating new-tab prerender targets

`PrerenderWebContentsDelegate::ActivateContents()` had `NOTREACHED()`,
assuming browser UI would never try to activate a hidden prerender tab.

However, DevTools now exposes new-tab prerenders as inspectable page
targets. Tools like ChromeDriver send `Target.activateTarget` when
switching or cleaning up windows, calling `ActivateContents()` and
crashing `headless_shell`.

This CL makes `ActivateContents()` a no-op, matching `TakeFocus()`.
Because background prerenders have no window to foreground, ignoring
the activation request is safe and avoids crashing external DevTools
and WebDriver sessions.

Over the last 7 days, this caused ~2,600 Linux CQ failures and 27 flake
exonerations in speculation-rules WPTs.

[bedrock]: Match standalone PiP origin chip styling

UI differences in the origin chip were caught in crrev.com/c/8453402.
This is to merge that gap between the standalone Document PiP origin
chip and the Browser-backed one.

- Label color: LocationIconView asks its delegate for the security-chip
  color. PictureInPictureBrowserFrameView returns
  kColorOmniboxSecurityChipSecure (kColorOmniboxSecurityChipText for
  "Dangerous"). The standalone chip used the top-bar foreground color
  instead, so its label was white and followed the active/inactive fade.
- Padding: LocationIconView::UpdateBorder() uses
  LOCATION_BAR_PAGE_INFO_ICON_PADDING plus the extra trailing padding
  when the label is shown, or the dangerous-state padding. The
  standalone chip used the generic IconLabelBubbleView border.
- Label after animation: LocationIconView::ShouldShowLabelAfterAnimation()
  returns ShouldShowLabel(). The base implementation follows
  ShouldShowSeparator(), which is false for the chip, so an animated
  "Not secure" or "Dangerous" label collapsed back to the icon.

Give OriginChipView the same behavior. The security icon still follows
the top-bar fade, as in the Browser-backed frame.

Handle unaligned destinations in `AudioData::copyTo()`

This CL fixes an issue when interleaving or deinterleaving without
sample conversion in `AudioData::copyTo()`. The destination memory may
not be aligned to the sample type's size (e.g. a `DataView` with an odd
byte offset). In `CopyToInterleaved()` and `CopyToPlanar()`, calling
`reinterpret_cast` on it and writing through it is undefined behavior.

To fix this, write into an aligned temporary buffer when the destination
is not aligned, and copy its bytes over after, like
`ConvertToInterleaved()` already does. Aligned destinations are still
written to directly.

[PiP] Prevent UAF in EnterVideoPictureInPicture on Document PiP child

When a video inside a Document Picture-in-Picture child WebContents
requests video Picture-in-Picture (for example, from an iframe inside
the Document PiP window), BrowserWebContentsDelegate forwards the
request to PictureInPictureWindowManager::EnterVideoPictureInPicture.
Because the active DocumentPictureInPictureWindowControllerImpl's
GetWebContents() is the opener rather than the Document PiP child,
EnterVideoPictureInPicture called CloseWindowInternal() to close the
active Document PiP window before calling CreateWindowInternal() with
the requesting WebContents.

When a JavaScript dialog (such as alert()) is active in the Document PiP
window, RenderFrameHostImpl::IsPageReadyToBeClosed() returns true and
ClosePage() synchronously destroys the Document PiP child WebContents
inside CloseWindowInternal(), causing a browser-process
heap-use-after-free when CreateWindowInternal() subsequently uses the
freed WebContents pointer (and in callers on the stack owned by that
WebContents).

This CL fixes the issue with defense-in-depth: 1. In
PictureInPictureWindowManager::EnterVideoPictureInPicture, reject
   requests where web_contents is the active Document PiP child
   WebContents (GetChildWebContents() == web_contents) with
   PictureInPictureResult::kNotSupported before closing the existing
   window, matching Blink's policy that video PiP is disabled inside
   Document PiP windows.
2. Guard web_contents with a base::WeakPtr across CloseWindowInternal()
   in PictureInPictureWindowManager::EnterVideoPictureInPicture and
   across EnterPictureInPicture() in
   VideoPictureInPictureWindowControllerImpl::StartSession, returning
   kNotSupported if closing an existing PiP window synchronously
   destroys the requesting WebContents.

Verification:
- Reproduced the pre-fix crash in PictureInPictureWindowManagerTest
  when CloseWindowInternal() synchronously destroys the requesting
  WebContents.
- Verified all 24 tests in PictureInPictureWindowManagerTest.* pass
  with the fix, including two new regression tests
  (EnterVideoPipRejectedForDocumentPipChildWebContents and
  EnterVideoPipFromClosingWindowDoesNotUseFreedWebContents).

[Omnibox] Use GENERATED for AI Mode popup query submits

Queries submitted from the omnibox AI Mode popup opened with
PAGE_TRANSITION_LINK because the popup reused NTP composebox code. As a
result, ActorNavigationThrottle treated popup searches as link clicks
instead of user queries, failing to prompt "Leave site and end task?"
when an actor task was running.

This CL updates popup submits to use PAGE_TRANSITION_GENERATED, matching
the AI Mode button, @aimode, and regular omnibox searches.

• Use GENERATED for popup submits in
ContextualSearchboxHandler::OpenUrl, while keeping LINK for non-popup
callers (such as NTP).

• New tabs opened from popup submits are no longer treated as link
clicks. They stay in the current tab's group, but open at the end of the
group, or at the end of the tab strip if the tab has no group, instead
of next to the current tab. They also do not join the current tab's
contextual task when the side panel is open

• Add browser tests for typed and voice popup submits, verifying the
navigation transition when the search starts.

• Add an actor throttle unit test for GENERATED navigations.

[WebAudio] Allow GC of unconnected MediaStreamAudioSourceNode

`MediaStreamAudioSourceNode::HasPendingActivity()` previously returned
true unconditionally while the `AudioContext` was running. This
prevented Oilpan from garbage collecting unconnected, unreferenced
nodes and their audio stream sinks.

Mirroring the fix for `MediaElementAudioSourceNode` in
crrev.com/c/8434351, this CL updates `HasPendingActivity()` to check
`HasOutputsConnected()` while the context is running. It also removes
the legacy `NotifySourceNodeStartedProcessing()` call from `Create()`,
which otherwise retains a `scoped_refptr` to the handler in
`active_source_handlers_` for the lifetime of the context.

Connected nodes continue to stay alive during active playback.

[Mac] Trace input method activation call sites

Opening a browser window with an input method such as Japanese selected
can block the main thread while AppKit activates the input method for
the focused location bar. In a trace this wait is only an untraced gap
inside Widget::Show, so attributing it has needed a custom build.

Add trace events around the calls in which AppKit activates the input
method: the +[NSTextInputContext currentInputContext] query in
-[BridgedContentView needsUpdateWindows], and -[NSApp updateWindows],
which BrowserCrApplication now overrides only to trace it. There is no
behavior change.

Revert "Fix script scheduling, style blocking, and abort cleanup for HTMLStream"

This reverts commit f19d15d649bb5bb0f4b2359e5537eb37ce5957cf.

Reason for revert: Causing CI failure

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20Tests%20(dbg)(1)/134072/overview

Original change's description:
> Fix script scheduling, style blocking, and abort cleanup for HTMLStream
>
> Align HTMLDocumentParser, HTMLTreeBuilder, HTMLParserScriptRunner,
> ScriptLoader, and PendingScript with the WHATWG HTML spec for
> streaming fragment parsers:
> - Do not block streamed inline, parser-blocking, or defer scripts on
>   script-blocking stylesheets in the live target document.
> - Keep classic non-async, non-defer external scripts parser-blocking
>   (kParserBlocking) for the stream, and yield to the event loop before
>   executing deferred/module scripts at close().
> - Flush pending text (including kTextMode) at the end of each chunk and
>   before StopParsing(), so written text is in the DOM when write()
>   resolves and no text is left buffered in HTMLConstructionSite when a
>   writer is dropped, aborted, or its write() rejects.
> - On StopParsing() / Detach() for fragment parsers ("abort a parser",
>   fragment case), mark open <script> elements already-started, pop all
>   open elements so elements like <style> finish parsing children, and
>   cancel pending parser-blocking and deferred scripts, which also
>   unblocks rendering on them.
> - At EOF in the "text" insertion mode, mark an unclosed <script>
>   already-started for fragment parsers, so it never runs even if it is
>   later connected. The same step for the main document parser is a
>   web-visible behavior change (an unclosed <script src> at EOF currently
>   executes) and is left for a separate, flagged CL (see TODO).
>
> WPT coverage includes parser-blocking/defer/async script scheduling,
> abort unblocking rendering, bare text inserted before close(), and an
> unclosed <script> at close() being marked already-started. The
> parser-blocking script tests depend on the displaced reference node
> handling in crrev.com/c/8498307, which this CL is based on.

[Cast] Stop mirroring when a session has neither audio nor video

MirroringActivity::StartSession() derives the session type by
intersecting the sink capabilities with what the media source provides.
When the result has neither audio nor video (e.g. casting a screen
without audio to an audio-only sink), StartSession() returned early
without starting or stopping anything, leaving a route that never
streams and never ends.

Call StopMirroring() in that case so the route is torn down.

[Actor] Route ActorTask through ActorSurface and add surface API

ActorTask now tracks the pages it acts on by ActorSurfaceHandle instead
of tabs::TabHandle, as a step toward acting on pages without a tab.
Tab behavior is unchanged: every page today is a tab-backed surface.

ActorTask:
- controlled_tabs_, to_observe_tabs_ and last_actuated_tab_ are keyed by
  ActorSurfaceHandle. Enter/exit of actor control and content-discard
  handling work on the surface handle.
- WebContents are reached through ActorSurface::GetWebContents(). When
  the surface is already gone (e.g. its tab is closing), the WebContents
  recorded in the controlled state are used to exit actor control.
- Surface methods: AddActorSurface (now the real implementation instead
  of routing to AddTab), RemoveActorSurface, ObserveActorSurfaceOnce,
  HasActorSurface, IsActingOnActorSurface, OnActorSurfaceWillDetach,
  GetActorSurfaces, GetLastActedActorSurfaces and
  GetLastActuatedActorSurface. AddActorSurface and
  ObserveActorSurfaceOnce reject surfaces that are gone or belong to
  another profile.
- The TabHandle methods remain as wrappers over the surface methods for
  callers not yet migrated (tools, observations, UI, Android). AddTab
  and ObserveTabOnce keep their tab-based profile check, since a tab in
  a profile without an ActorKeyedService has no surface.
- GetTabs() and GetLastActedTabs() skip surfaces without a tab. A page
  the task keeps after its tab closes (LoadAndExtract's temporary tabs)
  is then reported only through the tool's own observation.

Callers moved to the surface API: ActorKeyedService (including a
headless lookup in GetActingActorTaskForWebContents), the navigation
throttle, the desktop tab strip tracker, GlicActorTaskManager, the
password change actuator, ChromeAutofillClient and
IdentityDialogController.

Tests: unit-test fixtures register their mock tabs with
ActorSurfaceRegistry, as real tabs do through TabFeatures, and
ActorTaskSurfaceTest covers controlling and observing a page through
its surface.

WebTransport: blink part of GetStats for SendStream

Replace the zero-valued WebTransportSendStream.getStats() stub with
actual send-stream statistics.

Track bytes written to the Mojo data pipe in Blink and query the network
service for bytes sent and acknowledged. Capture final network
statistics before streams are unregistered on graceful close, local
abort, or STOP_SENDING so getStats() remains useful after termination.

Combine concurrent requests and coordinate responses arriving on
different Mojo pipes. Retain weak references to recently forgotten
streams to apply late final statistics and resolve pending requests when
the transport disconnects.

[Blink] Expose ProgressEvent in service workers

The XHR specification exposes ProgressEvent to Window and Worker, but
Blink currently omits service workers. Expose the existing
implementation there behind ProgressEventInServiceWorker, enabled by
default with stable status while retaining a Finch kill switch.

Convert the constructor WPT to .any.js to cover Window, dedicated,
shared and service workers. Update the default and virtual/stable
service worker interface listings.

2419fc7fb1939b0abf46f4268d24b5b3cda3d4b4 [ diff ] 
[Media] Bind channel token reply to a WeakPtr in browser GPU factories

BrowserGpuVideoAcceleratorFactories::GetChannelToken() requests the
token through the GpuChannel remote of the shared GpuChannelHost and
binds base::Unretained(this) to the reply. That remote is not owned by
the factories object, so destroying the factories does not drop the
pending reply. ThumbnailMediaParserImpl destroys its factories when it
times out or fails, and a reply that arrives afterwards runs
OnChannelTokenReady() on a destroyed object.

Bind the reply to a WeakPtr instead, as
MojoGpuVideoAcceleratorFactories does for the same call.

20761ee85ff20e6d344db903e06a1f16997c18cc [ diff ] 
[Updater][Mojo] Harden Windows pipe IPC against disconnects and rejections

1. Stop retrying for 30 seconds in ConnectMojoImpl when a server
   connection is rejected (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, failed privilege /
   elevation verification, or E_ACCESSDENIED from CoCreateInstance),
   and set ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED when
   NamedPlatformChannel::CreateClientEndpoint fails
   VerifyServerPrivilege. Return
   base::expected<mojo::PlatformChannelEndpoint, ConnectToServerError>
   from ConnectToUpdateService and SelectUpdateServiceEndpoint, and only
   treat owner/privilege check failures as kRejected so transient
   process or token lookup errors continue to be retried.

   Behavior change: a system-scope client that is not elevated and
   connects to a legacy server that only serves the kDefault pipe, or to
   the system internal service, now fails immediately with kRejected
   instead of retrying for 30 seconds and then failing.
2. In mojo::core::ChannelWin:
   - Hold a keep_alive reference across StartOnIOThread() and handle
     synchronous WriteNextNoLock() failures by setting reject_writes_ =
     true so subsequent writes do not queue behind the failed message
     while ReadMore(0) reports the disconnection.
   - Use CancelIoEx(handle_, nullptr) instead of CancelIo in
     ShutDownOnIOThread, since Write() may issue WriteFile() from any
     thread and CancelIo only cancels I/O issued by the calling thread.
3. In mojo::PlatformChannelServer on Windows:
   - Export ConnectNamedPipeWithoutCompletionPacket from
     mojo/public/cpp/platform (deduplicating
     components/named_mojo_ipc_server) and use it during
     ConnectNamedPipe so late completions cannot queue stale completion
     packets to the IOCP after the pipe handle is handed to ChannelWin.
   - Use CancelIoEx(&connect_overlapped_) instead of CancelIo in
     ~ListenerImpl so pending ConnectNamedPipe operations are canceled
     even if the listener is destroyed on a different thread than
     Start().
   - In ListenerImpl::Start, stop the ObjectWatcher before closing
     connect_event_ on the failure paths, so the event is never closed
     while it is still being watched.

omnibox: Route Ask Google to the omnibox only with an AIM popup

When the ContextualTasksContextMenuRouteAskGoogleToOmnibox param is
on, Ask Google about this page opens the AIM composebox in the
omnibox. OmniboxEditModel::OpenComposeboxForAskG() sets the popup state
to kAim unconditionally, but since crrev.com/c/8521198 a window gets an
AIM popup presenter only when the profile is AIM and fusebox eligible.
For other profiles the state became kAim with no popup to show, which
trips ValidatePopupState() on debug builds. LUCI Bisection blamed
those failures on that CL.

Fall back to the side panel when the window has no AIM popup.
ShouldRouteAskGoogleToOmnibox() checks AIM eligibility but not whether
the window has an AIM popup, which also depends on the AIM popup
feature. Using ShouldCreateAimPopupPresenter() keeps the old routing
when the kOmniboxAimPopupRequireEligibility kill switch is off.

Make the profile fusebox eligible in the routing tests and enable the
AIM popup there, since Linux and ChromeOS bots run browser_tests with
it disabled. Add a test for the fallback with an AIM-eligible profile
and the AIM popup feature off.

Skip per-transaction AddressSorter::Sort() for non-AAAA DNS transactions

AddressSorter::Sort() is designed for RFC 3484 / RFC 6724 destination
address selection and requires at least one IPv6 address in the input
list. In the non-individual sort path (ExtractAddressResultsForSort()),
sorting is skipped completely when there are no IPv6 endpoints.

However, when sorting DNS transactions individually
(SortTransactionAndHandleResults()), HostResolverDnsTask invoked
AddressSorter::Sort() on every completed transaction with endpoints,
including DnsQueryType::A (IPv4-only) transactions. This caused:
- Unnecessary ThreadPool MayBlock() hops and
  WSAIoctl(SIO_ADDRESS_LIST_SORT) calls on Windows for IPv4-only
  transactions.
- Unnecessary UDP socket connect checks on POSIX and prefix-based
  reordering of IPv4 addresses that overrides DNS round-robin order.
- Holding PrioritizedDispatcher job slots while the redundant async
  sort is in flight.

Restrict SortTransactionAndHandleResults() to DnsQueryType::AAAA
transactions so that non-AAAA transactions complete immediately via
HandleTransactionResults() without calling AddressSorter::Sort().

[Multiple Requests] Store access token to removed from cache later

Currently, `access_token_` is never set in `PaymentsAccessTokenFetcher`
so it's always empty. When a 401 error is returned from the server (due
to a stale access token), `MultipleRequestPaymentsNetworkInterfaceBase`
handles the retry request by first fetching a new access token via
`GetAccessToken()` with `invalidate_old` as `true`. But because
`access_token_` is always empty, `RemoveAccessTokenFromCache()` cannot
be called which means subsequent retry requests will just call
`CreateAccessTokenFetcherForAccount()`, which internally maintains its
own cache and will return the same stale access token.

This CL sets `access_token_` in `AccessTokenFetchFinished()` and updates
the unit tests to fetch the initial token via `GetAccessToken()` instead
of `set_access_token_for_testing()`.

[HiC] Invalidate filters when an element moves into canvas

Typically compositor filter operations are not rebuilt unless the style
filter value changes, regardless of paint invalidation. With this change
compositor filter operations will be aggressively rebuilt whenever
content moves into a canvas.

[ios][actor] Submit form on followByEnter for text inputs in TypeTool

Synthetic untrusted Enter key events dispatched by TypeTool do not
trigger the browser's implicit form submission on <input> elements.

When followByEnter is true and the target leaf element is a text-field
HTMLInputElement (checked via isTextField from
//ios/web/public/js_messaging:util_scripts) associated with a <form>,
call leafElement.form.requestSubmit() after dispatching the synthetic
Enter key sequence if the Enter events were not canceled via
preventDefault().

[HiC] Fix backdrop-filter combined with mix-blend-mode

Skia does not apply the backdrop filter when there is a
blend mode also present on the layer, though it may depend
on exactly which blend mode. This was preventing CSS
backdrop-filter from functioning when a CSS mix-blend-mode
was also active.

Fix the issue by saving another layer for the blend mode.
The fix is complicated by the use of kDstIn blend mode to
implement masks, which still requires the blend mode on
the backdrop save layer.

parent
f06e49b0cd76f04a6233c5b22ae2fd52926bc598 [ diff ] 
[Extensions] Wait for SW re-registration on mismatch

When prefs record a registration for an extension's worker,
ActivateExtension() marks the worker as kRegistered, and verifies the
registration with //content asynchronously. If //content doesn't have
it, DidVerifyRegistration() registers the worker again, but leaves it
marked as kRegistered. Tasks then try to start a worker that //content
can't find: the starts fail with kErrorNotFound and are retried, and the
tasks fail once retries run out. If the registration fails, this happens
to every task until the extension is activated again.

Mark the worker as kRegistering during that registration, so that tasks
wait for it, and DidRegisterServiceWorker() starts the worker once it's
registered. Every caller of RegisterServiceWorker() now needs this, so
it sets kRegistering itself. If the registration fails, the worker is
marked as kNotRegistered, and its tasks wait until the extension is
deactivated, as after any other failed registration. A follow-up
addresses this.

A task added before the verification finishes may already have requested
a worker start, or scheduled a start retry. RegisterServiceWorker() now
also cancels start retries, and OnWorkerStartFail() leaves the tasks
queued while the worker isn't registered, instead of retrying the start.
Otherwise, the retry would hit the CHECK in RetryStartWorker().

[glic] Add Glic.Instance.TimeToActionable histogram

Adds `Glic.Instance.TimeToActionable.{Inactive.}{EmbedderType}` while
retaining `Glic.Instance.PanelPresentationTime.{Inactive.}{EmbedderType}`
unchanged (with its histogram summary clarified to state that it is
recorded at most once per instance on the web client's ready signal).

`Glic.Instance.TimeToActionable.{Inactive.}{EmbedderType}` measures the
duration from an explicit invocation (`OnOpen`) to when the guest emits
the `"gemini.interactive"` user timing performance mark and its next
compositor frame is submitted (`InsertVisualStateCallback`) while the
panel is visible and the guest is mounted (or immediately at the mark
timestamp under the `Inactive.` variant if the panel is already hidden
when the mark arrives).

Because the `"gemini.interactive"` mark observer and visual state
callback are always active (not gated behind `kGlicSsr`), this histogram
is recorded in both control and enabled arms whenever the guest emits
the mark, and is tracked per guest document so subsequent opens after a
guest reload, crash, or hibernate are also timed.

parent
8d3b6a9bdef4d58ee6d7b4a8ab73907f60ac456b [ diff ] 
printing: Pass the print FD and settings directly at onWrite

Android previously passed the destination file descriptor and print
parameters from Java to C++ through reverse JNI getters called during
AskUserForSettings(), smuggling the raw descriptor into
PrintSettings::device_name as a stringified integer and writing the PDF
synchronously on the UI thread with ambiguous descriptor ownership.

Pass the detached ParcelFileDescriptor and print settings directly
forward from PrintSession#onWrite to
PrintViewManagerBasic::PrintNowAndroid(). PrintViewManagerBasic now owns
the ScopedFD and PrintSettings for the active job, validates renderer
IPC senders against the printing frame and cookie, writes the PDF
asynchronously on a worker thread, and releases the descriptor
unconditionally on completion or failure. The asynchronous completions
carry the job's document cookie, so a write that finishes after
FinishPrint() cannot reset the state of a job that was started after it.

[Reading Mode] Don't print the line focus scroll buffer

Static line focus pads the top and bottom of the Reading Mode content by
half the height of the reading area, so that the first and last lines
can scroll to the middle of the screen.

However, printing IRM kept that padding, so the printout started with a
blank band.

Remove the padding when printing, so that the printout is laid out the
same whether line focus is on or off.

🌺 Guard SmartSelectionCallback against destroyed WebContents

On chrome/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests (where fieldtrial_testing_config
is not enabled by default, so sTextClassifierTimeout is false),
PopupWindowTest#testPopupWindowTextHandle and the subsequent batched test
PopupWindowTest#testDefaultUserAgentsInParentAndChildWindows have been
failing in 12 of the last 14 builds (#5278..#5291), e.g.:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests/5291

Root cause:
1. When AiAiTextClassifier on the device cold-starts, SystemTextClassifier
   takes ~3.01s to respond, exceeding the default 3000ms timeout in
   PopupWindowTest.assertWaitForSelectActionBarStatus().
2. When testPopupWindowTextHandle tears down, popupContents (WebContents)
   is destroyed natively: SmartSelectionClient.onNativeSideDestroyed()
   cancels ClassificationTask, and SelectionPopupControllerImpl.destroyFromNative()
   resets mNativeSelectionPopupController = 0 without clearing mHasSelection.
3. On the next UI thread turn, ClassificationTask.onCancelled() invokes
   SmartSelectionCallback.onClassifiedLate(), which only checked
   hasSelection() and called populateMenu() -> isIncognito() ->
   WebContentsImpl.checkNotDestroyed(), crashing the process with
   IllegalStateException: Native WebContents already destroyed.

Fix:
- Guard SmartSelectionCallback.onClassified() and onClassifiedLate() with
  mWebContents.isDestroyed() and mContext == null checks, and clear
  mHasSelection and mClassificationResult in destroyFromNative().
- Pass AwActivityTestRule.WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS to CriteriaHelper.pollUiThread
  in PopupWindowTest.assertWaitForSelectActionBarStatus().

Reland "[glic] Start benchmark: remove harness artifacts from the cold number"

This is a reland of commit b0abae75dc17492cfe174713d8b92301277c80ed

On Mobile Android (!IS_DESKTOP_ANDROID), neither kSitePerProcess nor
kAndroidWarmUpSpareRendererWithTimeout is enabled by default in
production, so Glic opens without a spare renderer. Disable the
fieldtrial_testing_config.json kAndroidWarmUpSpareRendererWithTimeout
study on Mobile Android so the benchmark measures its real no-spare
behavior rather than warming a one-off spare after the warmup tab loads,
and use std::ranges::all_of when waiting for pending spares so platforms
or bots with no spare in flight proceed without hanging.

Original change's description:
> [glic] Start benchmark: remove harness artifacts from the cold number
>
> The default HTTP/1 EmbeddedTestServer closes the connection after every
> response, so each guest script fetch paid a TCP+TLS handshake;
> production serves the client over one HTTP/2 connection. The test client
> also imported WebClientMode as a value, pulling the 46 KB generated API
> into a three-deep import waterfall that production never fetches. And a
> fresh test browser paid network-service initialization on the first
> open.
>
> Serve the guest from an H2 server (new
> GlicBrowserTestMixin::set_glic_https_test_server() hook; other fixtures
> are unchanged), make the client's API imports type-only with
> modulepreload for the remaining two files, and warm the network service
> with one navigation to a separate origin before the timer. The guest
> origin is left cold on purpose: Chrome does not preconnect for Glic, so
> its DNS/TCP/TLS is real cold-open cost. Also wait for a ready spare
> renderer before timing, log nav/resource timing per iteration, and have
> run_glic_start_benchmark.py report cold and warm separately.
>

[update_client] Fix the DO downloader never completing a download

Running the DeliveryOptimizationDownloader against a real Delivery
Optimization service on the Windows try bots showed that it could not
complete a download on a machine where it had not run before, for three
independent reasons, fixed here:

1. IDOManager::EnumDownloads reports an empty queue as DO_E_NO_DOWNLOADS
   rather than by returning an empty enumerator. FindDownloadsIf treated
   that as a failure, which QueueDownload then folded into
   CrxDownloaderError::DO_TOO_MANY_DOWNLOADS, so the very first download
   on any machine failed before DO was even asked to create it. Treat
   DO_E_NO_DOWNLOADS as "no downloads found", and return the actual
   HRESULT for other enumeration failures so that the real cause shows
   up in telemetry.

2. DO creates and writes the download file on the caller's behalf, which
   requires the COM proxies to allow impersonation. The browser does not
   call CoInitializeSecurity, so the process-wide default of
   RPC_C_IMP_LEVEL_IDENTIFY applied, and IDODownload::Start failed with
   HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_DIRECTORY) regardless of the download
   location. Set an RPC_C_IMP_LEVEL_IMPERSONATE blanket on the
   IDOManager and IDODownload proxies.

3. A transferred download holds its content in the DO cache; the file at
   the local path only appears once the download is finalized.
   CompleteDownload checked for the file before calling Finalize and so
   always failed with E_UNEXPECTED. Check for the file after finalizing.

Also add VLOG(1) output at the points where the DO interaction can fail,
which is what made the above diagnosable from the bot logs.

Verified with the DeliveryOptimizationDownloaderIntegrationTest suite
from the follow-up CL on the win-rel try bot.

[Safe Browsing] Check NavigationHandle::HasUserGesture in NavigationObserver

When a user clicks a link inside a cross-origin iframe (OOP-iframe),
RenderWidgetHostImpl::OnUserInputEvent returns early when
!IsOutermostMainFrame(), so WebContentsObserver::DidGetUserInteraction
is not called and SafeBrowsingNavigationObserver's per-WebContents user
gesture map does not record the gesture. However, Blink still notifies
the browser of transient user activation on the frame, which sets
NavigationHandle::HasUserGesture() to true.

Check navigation_handle->HasUserGesture() in
SafeBrowsingNavigationObserver::SetNavigationInitiationAndRecordUserGesture
so renderer-initiated navigations with a user gesture on the
NavigationHandle are recorded as RENDERER_INITIATED_WITH_USER_GESTURE.

Pass byte_offset instead of raw pointer to AVC::FindSubsampleIndex

Replace the `buffer` and `const uint8_t* ptr` parameters on
`FindSubsampleIndex` with `size_t byte_offset`, since
`FindSubsampleIndex` only used `buffer` to compute `ptr - buffer.data()`
and callers already have an offset or iterator into `buffer`.

Also extract `AVC::InsertParamSetsIntoBuffer` to share the subsample
update and insertion logic between `AVC::InsertParamSetsAnnexB` and
`HEVC::InsertParamSetsAnnexB`, which ports the end-of-buffer insertion
check from crrev.com/c/1366878 (crbug.com/40605149) to HEVC as well, and
make `FindSubsampleIndex` an internal helper in `avc.cc` with
`AVC::FindSubsampleIndexForTesting` on the public interface.

[WebUI Omnibox] Keep caret on clicked character when uneliding URL

Problem: In the WebUI omnibox popup, clicking a second time in a
focused, fully-selected elided URL (e.g. "facebook.com") unelides it to
the full URL (e.g. "https://www.facebook.com/"), shifting the text to
the right. The caret then lands at the raw mouse X coordinate in the
shifted text (e.g. inside the newly shown "https://") instead of on the
character the user clicked, unlike the Views omnibox.

Root cause: `onInputMousedown_()` unelided the URL synchronously in the
`mousedown` handler, before Blink's default handling hit-tests the
click. Blink therefore placed the caret against the already-unelided
layout.

Fix: Match `OmniboxViewViews`, where pressing inside the selection
leaves it intact (it may start a drag-and-drop of the URL), and release
places the caret at the release point (`views::SelectionController::
OnMouseReleased()`) before `UnapplySteadyStateElisions()` unelides and
shifts the selection by the elided prefix:
- On `mousedown`, keep the URL elided and the selection intact, so
  dragging still drag-and-drops the selected URL.
- On `mouseup`, place the caret at the character under the (clamped)
  release point using `document.caretPositionFromPoint()`. Blink would
  only do so after `mouseup` is dispatched, and not at all if the
  pointer moved. Then unelide and shift the selection by the length of
  the elided prefix. Unlike Views, selections starting at the beginning
  of the elided URL are not extended over the elided prefix, for
  simplicity.
- On `dragstart`, cancel the pending unelision, since Blink dispatches
  no `mouseup` after a drag. A keydown during the press (e.g.
  Cmd/Ctrl+L) cancels it too, like the pending select-all on release.
  Other paths (multi-clicks, clicks outside the text, keyboard) are
  unchanged.

[Media] Support native D3D12 picture buffers

D3DPictureBuffer previously assumed every decode target originated as a
D3D11 texture and required conversion through a shared handle before
D3D12 decode could use it.

With this CL, we now allow picture buffers to own either a D3D11 texture
or a native D3D12 resource. We also let the D3D12 decoder wrapper
consume native resources directly while retaining shared-handle
conversion for D3D11-backed fallback paths. The shared-handle code will
be deleted after the introduction of a D3D12 Video Decoder Backend.

This removes D3D11-specific assumptions from picture-buffer users and
prepares the decoder backend to allocate D3D12 output resources
natively.

[TabUI] Move requiresThumbnailUpdateOnDeselect to TabListConfig

Whether a tab list layout requires refreshing a card's thumbnail when a
tab is deselected (such as multi-thumbnail group cards and deselected
live tabs in the Grid Tab Switcher) is a static layout capability rather
than dynamic delegate state. Move `requiresThumbnailUpdateOnDeselect`
from `TabListLayoutDelegate` into `TabListConfig` so `TabListMediator`
can read it directly from `mTabListConfig` without routing through
`TabListLayoutDelegate`. This is a no-op refactoring with no behavior
change.

chrome: Mark internal browser captures as secure

See design doc at http://shortn/_8FWRuV0PVg. This is part 3 of the CLs.

To ensure secure internal browser UI features are not redacted when
video capture protection is enabled, this CL marks internal captures
on desktop as secure:
1. Lens Overlay / Contextual Search screenshot and blur layer captures.
2. Tab Hover Cards / background thumbnail capture.
3. Tab Dragging thumbnails.
4. Mirroring / Cast video capture.

Unit test is added in openscreen_session_host_unittest.cc to verify
MirrorSettings sets is_secure to true.

[ash] Don't re-show transient window being destroyed

`MultiUserWindowManager::RemoveTransientOwnerRecursive()` removes a
window and its descendants from transient-tracking. For all those
windows, it tries to restore their visibility to what it was prior to
being hidden by their transient owner. E.g. if window A owns transient
child B, and window B was hidden because A was hidden, then detaching B
should restore B's visibility.

However, detaching also happens when a window is being destroyed. E.g.
when window B is being destroyed, it calls
`RemoveTransientOwnerRecursive()` to detach itself. Attempting to
restore visibility on a window being destroyed causes a `CHECK()` crash.

Repro steps:
1. On ChromeOS, sign into two user accounts.
2. In User 1, open a website that requests a permission and reloads
   after a few second delay.
3. While the permission window is open, press Ctrl+Alt+. to switch to
   User 2.
4. Wait for the background tab on User 1 to reload.

This causes the permission prompt to be destroyed, which calls
`RemoveTransientOwnerRecursive()`, which tries to re-show the dying
window, which crashes.

Fix:
`RemoveTransientOwnerRecursive()` will not restore visibility on windows
that are being destroyed.

`MultiUserWindowManager` is chromeOS specific.

TAG=agy
CONV=c16bc7a5-b01d-4951-8765-8316f70b073c

Add ui::ScopedSetSelectFileDialogFactory to restore factory on exit

Add ui::ScopedSetSelectFileDialogFactory in //ui/shell_dialogs to set
SelectFileDialogFactory for the duration of its lifetime and restore the
previously set factory upon destruction.

This is needed for tests: content::ScopedSelectFileDialogFactory resets
the factory to nullptr upon destruction, which drops any pre-existing
production factory (e.g., Ash, headless). This CL is a preparation for
fixing that on the test caller side, which is done by the next CL
(crrev.com/c/8528927).

Add unit tests in ui/shell_dialogs/select_file_dialog_unittest.cc.

[Actor] Remove Tool::GetTargetTab()

Pure mechanical follow-up to crrev.com/c/8522700. All tools now report
their target through GetTargetActorSurface(), which is now pure virtual.

- ChangePassword and Wait now store their target ActorSurfaceHandle.
- Tab-based tools (TabManagement, SwitchTab, OpenKnownPage) keep
  operating on tabs and convert to a surface handle in
  GetTargetActorSurface().
- Tools without a target (Bookmark, Window, LoadAndExtractContent,
  Fake) return a null handle.
- Remove the tab fallback in ToolController::ValidateTarget().

This CL simplifies `AppInfoDialog` by setting its borders once at
construction. Previously, this view was required to manually handle
theme updates by overriding `OnThemeChanged()`.

management.

Prevent Range::expand() from crossing shadow boundaries

Range::expand() computes word, sentence, block, and document boundaries
using editing position utilities that can traverse the flat tree across
shadow boundaries and return positions in a different TreeScope. Passing
those unadjusted positions to Range::setStart() and Range::setEnd()
causes the Range to collapse into the target shadow tree, exposing nodes
inside closed or user-agent shadow roots.

Adjust the positions in Range::expand() so that they remain within the
Range's initial TreeScope, clamping positions that cross into a child
shadow tree to before or after the shadow host and clamping positions
that cross out of a shadow tree to the start or end of the shadow root.

settings: Defer showing main settings when state is saved

Showing main settings in single-column mode pops the detail back stack
in MultiColumnSettings.onCreateInitialDetailFragment(). FragmentManager
refuses popBackStack() once its state is saved, so when a settings tab
whose URL resolves to main settings is restored after
ChromeTabbedActivity has already saved its instance state,
SettingsPageFragmentDelegateImpl.updateForUrl() ->
SettingsHostFragment.showFragment(null) crashes with the same
IllegalStateException in FragmentManager.checkStateLoss() that
https://crrev.com/c/8547513 fixed for detail pages. That fix is in
showDetailFragment(), which this path does not reach.

Defer the request through the same pending intent that
showDetailFragment() uses, naming MainSettings, and have
MultiColumnSettings.onResume() replay it via showFragment(null). Since
both kinds of request share the one pending slot, the latest request
wins without any extra bookkeeping. Deferring the whole request also
keeps its two-column closePane() undo (https://crbug.com/563047017)
running after the pane is opened rather than before.

WebNN: Fix OS driver version lookup in EP metadata

GetOsDriverVersion() compared the metadata key with raw const char*
pointers, comparing addresses instead of contents, so it never
matched and the driver version was always empty. Wrap the key in
std::string_view to compare by content.

This fixes a bug introduced by the recently landed
https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8534651.

[Actor] Register ActivateTabToolRequest in ToolRegistry

ToolRegistry provides a central catalog of browser tool schemas for
ActorKeyedService (go/actor-tool-registry-design). ToolRequest subclasses
expose their schema via static GetToolDefinition(), and ToolRegistry
discovers them at compile time through ToolRequestVariant.

This CL registers ActivateTabToolRequest in ToolRegistry by adding
ToolId::kActivateTab, declaring kModelFacingName ("activate_tab"), and
implementing GetToolDefinition() with required tab_id parameter. It also
adds unit test coverage in tool_registry_unittest.cc under desktop build
guards, since tab_management_tool_request.h is excluded from Android.

[context-input] Use QueryContextualizer for extension handler submit

ContextualTasksWebContentsUserData now submits via
QueryContextualizer::Contextualize(), like
ContextualTasksComposeboxHandler, and posts the OnSubmitQueryResponse
once it completes.

Delayed (auto-suggested chip) tabs are no longer snapshotted when
added. The session handle records them via the new
AddPendingDelayedTab(), and the contextualizer captures and uploads
them at submit, so the snapshot plumbing is removed. Pending delayed
tabs are selected and report a READY context state. The extension UI
currently always passes delayUpload=false, so this does not change
current behavior.

AddDelayedTabContext() is renamed to AttachTabPendingUpload() to
reflect its remaining uses.

Deleting a chip goes through the new session handle
DeleteTabContext(), which unlike DeleteFile() also deletes the tab's
current token if an upload replaced the chip's token.

settings: Fix IllegalStateException in exitSearchState

When SettingsSearchCoordinator#exitSearchState is called from
onTitleUpdated() during FragmentLifecycleCallbacks#onFragmentResumed(),
FragmentManager is already executing transactions. Calling
commitNowAllowingStateLoss() to remove search fragments in that callback
throws IllegalStateException("FragmentManager is already executing
transactions"). Use commitAllowingStateLoss() instead, which still runs
before the asynchronous popBackStack() call that follows.

Also restore the FS_SEARCH state when SearchResultsPreferenceFragment
resumes while in FS_RESULTS (for example, when ManageSyncSettings
finishes itself on sign-out and pops the back stack directly without
going through stepBackInResultState()).

[ContextualTasks] Bound extension handshake by wall-clock time

The extension frame's handshake gave up after MAX_HANDSHAKE_ATTEMPTS
pings, but pings are suppressed until a target origin resolves, so a
frame with an unusable referrer kept a 10ms interval running for its
whole lifetime. Stop the handshake HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS (30s) of
wall-clock time after it starts instead. This also keeps throttled
timers in hidden frames from stretching the budget well past 30s.

WebXR: Tolerate incomplete plane detection updates

XRPlaneManager assumes that plane IDs omitted from updated plane data are already present in its cache. After tracking data is temporarily unavailable, the cache can be cleared before the device resumes sending unchanged IDs. This causes a renderer CHECK failure.

Ignore IDs that have neither updated data nor a cached XRPlane. A subsequent complete update can recreate the plane normally. This keeps malformed or temporarily inconsistent device deltas from terminating the renderer.

Test: third_party/blink/tools/run_web_tests.py --no-xvfb --no-show-results --no-manifest-update --additional-driver-flag=--headless=new -t Default external/wpt/webxr/plane-detection/

Bug: none


WebXR: Handle infinite far planes in projection matrices

WebXR permits depthFar to be positive infinity. The existing projection calculations divide by near - far and later multiply the result by far. When far is infinity, this produces NaN entries in the projection matrix.

Calculate the depth scale and translation separately before constructing the matrix. For an infinite far plane, use the analytical limits required by each clip-space convention:

WebGL [-1, 1]: z_scale = -1, z_translate = -2 * near
WebGPU [0, 1]: z_scale = -1, z_translate = -near
Apply this handling to both field-of-view and aspect-based projection calculations. Keep the existing finite-far formulas unchanged.

Add focused coverage for WebGL and WebGPU through both projection paths. Each test checks the complete matrix and verifies that every component is finite. Retain finite-far coverage to guard against changes to existing projection results.

parent

[Glic] Release the microphone when the Android panel is not in front

Gemini voice input kept listening after Chrome left the foreground, for
example when the user switched apps or answered an incoming call. On
return the input could stay stuck in the listening state.

The Glic bottom sheet WebContents never changed page visibility. The
thin web view marks it visible once when it attaches, and nothing hid
it when the activity stopped, so the page never got a visibilitychange
event. The bottom sheet web UI now observes the host activity, the same
way tabs do: it hides the WebContents when the activity stops and shows
it again on resume. It also hides a WebContents attached while the
activity is already stopped.

The Android side panel embedder now asks the web client to stop the
microphone when the hosting window loses focus to another app or
system UI, and when the sheet closes, peeks, or hides for a tab switch.
Focus loss caused by a microphone permission prompt does not stop it,
and the late deactivation sent after such a prompt does not either,
because activation can lag the end of the OS prompt.

[remoting] Set default-terminal to xterm-256color for CRD tmux sessions

tmx2 defaults to TERM=tmux-256color inside panes, which does not match
the standard Debian/gLinux ~/.bashrc case statement (xterm*|rxvt*) for
emitting OSC 0 terminal title escape sequences in PS1.

Setting default-terminal to xterm-256color in the outer CRD tmux
persistence wrapper ensures shells automatically update the terminal tab
title when changing directories or returning to the prompt.

This is similar to many of the other options we set, which are largely
intended to mask the fact that tmux is being used.

settings: Drop the stale main menu key from the toolbar shortcut page

AdaptiveToolbarSettingsFragment declares "toolbar_shortcut" as its
main menu row, but that row moved into Appearance when the
AndroidAppearanceSettings flag was removed. Under SettingsInTabUrlNav,
opening chrome://settings/toolbar in two-column mode therefore
highlighted no row, since a declared key short-circuits the breadcrumb
lookup and this one matches nothing.

crrev.com/c/8490574 works around this by ignoring declared keys whose
row is not on the main menu, but it is intended to be reverted once
the stale overrides are cleaned up (crbug.com/513493349). Drop this
one so the page resolves its row through the breadcrumb trail, which
places it under Appearance.

ed5d38477cec29006f3d71c1dfba0aa2b4a43ed1 [ diff ] 
[COEP] Deflake reporting-subresource-corp.https.html

reporting-subresource-corp.https.html has been flaking with both
timeouts and unexpected assertion failures on debug and Mac bots:

1. resources/reporting-worker.js started a 200ms setTimeout before
evaluating the fetch() script and unconditionally disconnected the
ReportingObserver when the timer fired. On slower bots, cross-origin or
redirected worker fetches and ReportingObserver delivery can take longer
than 200ms, causing the worker to return fewer reports than expected.

2. observeReports() in reporting-subresource-corp.https.html
unconditionally slept 500ms in every subtest even after receiving all
expected reports (adding 5.5s of fixed sleep across the 11 frame/script
subtests), and started the timer before fetch() completed when
expected_count == 0.

Fix this by awaiting the evaluated script in reporting-worker.js and
waiting for expected_count reports when expected_count > 0 (only using
the 200ms settle wait when expected_count is 0 or unspecified), and by
awaiting the fetch promise in observeReports() and skipping the extra
delay once expected_count > 0 reports have arrived. Remove the [ Pass
Timeout ] entry from TestExpectations.

adds ActorEnterprisePolicyChecker::AddUrlListsUpdateObserver so

same-line backward-X jumps between left-to-right runs in
`LineHelper::ContinuesLineInReadingOrder()` and
`BreakParagraphByLineSpacing()` so side-by-side columns emitted out of
reading order are not merged into a single line or paragraph.
